questions.prompt: What must a synchronous ValidatorFn return?

options.text: null when valid, or a ValidationErrors object when invalid

questions.explanation: A ValidatorFn is (control) => ValidationErrors | null; null means valid, an errors object describes what failed.

questions.prompt: Why must an async validator's Observable complete?

options.text: Otherwise it uses too much memory
Angular waits for completion to move the control out of PENDING; a non-completing stream leaves it pending forever

questions.explanation: Use first() or take(1) (or rely on HttpClient completing) so the control can resolve to VALID/INVALID.

options.text: A service that stores all validators
A function that returns a ValidatorFn/AsyncValidatorFn, so the rule can be parameterized and reused

questions.explanation: Factories like minAgeValidator(18) return a configured validator, keeping rules reusable across the app.

questions.prompt: While an async validator is running, what is the control's status?
questions.explanation: PENDING means 'I don't know yet' — neither valid nor invalid — so the UI can show a 'checking…' state.

questions.prompt: Which techniques keep an async validator that checks the server while the user types efficient and resilient? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Start the request from timer(400) so quick typing never reaches the server
switchMap from the timer to the HTTP request
catchError so a failed check does not block the form

questions.explanation: Angular unsubscribes from the previous validation on every value change, so a short timer acts as a debounce and switchMap starts the request. distinctUntilChanged has no effect inside a validator, because each call creates a stream with a single value.

questions.prompt: Where should a validator that compares two sibling fields be attached?

options.text: On one of the individual FormControls
On the parent FormGroup (or FormArray), which can read both via group.get()

questions.explanation: A single control can't read its siblings; cross-field checks belong on the group that contains them.
